# RE Non-zero F1 Conditional Selection Analysis

**Experiment**: exp_012_rerun_1024 (Qwen SciERC joint NER+RE, N=8, seed=42, max_tokens=1024)
**Date**: 2026-05-15

## Dataset Statistics

| Metric | Count | Pct |
|--------|-------|-----|
| Total instances | 551 | 100% |
| Non-zero RE greedy F1 | 238 | 43.2% |
| Zero RE greedy F1 | 313 | 56.8% |

Over half of the instances have greedy RE F1 = 0 (no correct relations extracted).

## Selection Performance — Full Set (n=551)

| Signal | Selected F1 | Greedy F1 | Oracle F1 | Gain | p-value |
|--------|------------|-----------|-----------|------|---------|
| LP | 0.2845 | 0.2913 | 0.4215 | -0.0068 | 1.000 |
| FK | 0.2789 | 0.2913 | 0.4215 | -0.0123 | 1.000 |
| SJ | 0.2777 | 0.2913 | 0.4215 | -0.0135 | 1.000 |
| VC | 0.2588 | 0.2913 | 0.4215 | -0.0325 | 1.000 |
| EM | 0.2679 | 0.2913 | 0.4215 | -0.0233 | 1.000 |

## Selection Performance — Non-zero F1 Subset (n=238)

| Signal | Selected F1 | Greedy F1 | Oracle F1 | Gain | p-value |
|--------|------------|-----------|-----------|------|---------|
| LP | 0.5995 | 0.6743 | 0.7574 | -0.0748 | 1.000 |
| FK | 0.6063 | 0.6743 | 0.7574 | -0.0680 | 1.000 |
| SJ | 0.6035 | 0.6743 | 0.7574 | -0.0708 | 1.000 |
| VC | 0.5737 | 0.6743 | 0.7574 | -0.1005 | 1.000 |
| EM | 0.5828 | 0.6743 | 0.7574 | -0.0914 | 1.000 |

## Comparison: Full vs Non-zero

| Signal | Full Gain | Non-zero Gain | Delta |
|--------|-----------|---------------|-------|
| LP | -0.0068 | -0.0748 | -0.0680 |
| FK | -0.0123 | -0.0680 | -0.0557 |
| SJ | -0.0135 | -0.0708 | -0.0573 |
| VC | -0.0325 | -0.1005 | -0.0680 |
| EM | -0.0233 | -0.0914 | -0.0681 |

## Conclusion

**Zero-F1 instances are NOT masking good selection performance.** The opposite is true:

1. **All 5 signals fail to beat greedy** on both full and non-zero subsets (all gains negative, all p=1.0).

2. **Non-zero subset is worse, not better.** Selection gain magnitudes are 5-10x larger (more negative) on the non-zero subset. On the full set, zero-F1 instances dilute the damage because signal-based selection on zero-F1 instances often picks another zero-F1 sample (no harm done). On the non-zero subset, greedy is already strong (F1=0.6743), and signals actively pick inferior samples.

3. **Oracle gap remains large** (0.7574 vs 0.6743 on non-zero subset), confirming there is room for improvement — but current signals cannot exploit it. The signals are not just noisy; they are anti-correlated with quality for RE.

4. **VC and EM are the worst selectors**, with gains of -0.1005 and -0.0914 on the non-zero subset, likely because majority voting and exact match favor conservative (fewer relations) outputs that happen to miss correct relations.

**Data**: Qwen SciERC joint (NER+RE), N=8, seed=42, max_tokens=1024, 551 instances

---

## 1. Logprob Range Distribution

Mean logprob range (max−min across 8 samples per instance):

| Statistic | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Mean | 0.0623 |
| Median | 0.0413 |
| P25 | 0.0265 |
| P75 | 0.0693 |
| P90 | 0.1221 |
| P95 | 0.1770 |
| Max | 0.6083 |

**Logprob 值极度集中**：median range 仅 0.041，意味着一半 instance 的 8 个样本 mean_logprob 差异不到 0.04。

## 2. Tie 比例 vs ε 阈值

| ε (range < ε = "tied") | Tied instances | 比例 |
|------------------------|----------------|------|
| 0.001 | 6/551 | 1.1% |
| 0.005 | 8/551 | 1.5% |
| 0.01 | 11/551 | 2.0% |
| 0.02 | 78/551 | 14.2% |
| **0.05** | **329/551** | **59.7%** |
| 0.10 | 461/551 | 83.7% |
| 0.20 | 532/551 | 96.6% |
| 0.50 | 548/551 | 99.5% |

**关键发现**：以 ε=0.05 为标准，**60% 的 instance logprob 值几乎无差异**，选择退化为近似随机。

## 3. 整体 Selection Performance

| Strategy | NER F1 | RE F1 |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Greedy | 0.6436 | 0.4909 |
| Random sample (mean) | 0.6059 | — |
| **Logprob-best** | **0.6495** | 0.4442 |
| Logprob-worst | 0.5098 | — |
| Oracle | 0.7775 | — |

Logprob-best 在 NER 上仅比 greedy 高 +0.006，Oracle gap 高达 +0.13，说明 selection 远未饱和。

## 4. Non-Tied 子集上的 Selection Performance

| 阈值 (range ≥) | N (占比) | Greedy F1 | LP-best F1 | Diff | p-value | Win/Lose/Tie |
|---------------|----------|-----------|------------|------|---------|-------------|
| 0.01 | 540 (98%) | 0.6407 | 0.6463 | +0.006 | 0.422 | 60/70/410 |
| 0.02 | 473 (86%) | 0.6276 | 0.6356 | +0.008 | 0.289 | 56/61/356 |
| **0.05** | **222 (40%)** | **0.5863** | **0.6133** | **+0.027** | **0.010** | 29/20/173 |
| 0.10 | 90 (16%) | 0.5680 | 0.6029 | +0.035 | 0.079 | 13/8/69 |
| 0.20 | 19 (3%) | 0.6649 | 0.7108 | +0.046 | 0.295 | 4/1/14 |

**核心结论**：在 logprob 有足够区分度的子集 (range ≥ 0.05, 40% data) 上，logprob selection **显著优于** greedy (p=0.01)。随着区分度增大，logprob 优势单调递增 (+0.027 → +0.035 → +0.046)。

## 5. Within-Instance Logprob-F1 Correlation

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Mean Spearman ρ (mean_logprob ↔ NER F1) | 0.1823 |
| Median ρ | 0.2852 |
| % positive ρ | 64.3% |

Stratified by logprob range:

| Range bin | N instances | Mean ρ | N with variance |
|-----------|------------|--------|----------------|
| < 0.01 | 11 | +0.319 | 4 |
| 0.01–0.05 | 318 | +0.084 | 255 |
| 0.05–0.1 | 132 | +0.252 | 110 |
| **0.1–0.5** | **87** | **+0.390** | 76 |
| ≥ 0.5 | 3 | +0.506 | 3 |

**Logprob 信号随区分度增大而显著增强**：range 在 0.1-0.5 时 ρ=0.39，说明 logprob 本身包含质量信号，但被极窄的数值范围压缩了。

## 6. Structural Consistency (SJ) vs Logprob 对比

### 整体

| Strategy | NER F1 |
|----------|--------|
| Greedy | 0.6436 |
| Logprob-best | 0.6495 |
| SJ-best | 0.6505 |
| Oracle | 0.7775 |

### Non-tied 子集

| Subset | Greedy | LP-best | SJ-best | SJ vs LP (p) |
|--------|--------|---------|---------|--------------|
| range ≥ 0.05 (N=222) | 0.5863 | **0.6133** | 0.6066 | -0.007, p=0.62 |
| range ≥ 0.1 (N=90) | 0.5680 | **0.6029** | 0.5659 | -0.037, p=0.12 |

**意外发现**：在 logprob non-tied 子集上，logprob selection 实际 **优于** SJ。说明 logprob 在有足够 spread 时是有效的 quality signal。

### Tie 对比

| Signal | Tied 比例 | 定义 |
|--------|----------|------|
| Logprob (range < 0.05) | **59.7%** | 数值压缩严重 |
| SJ (range ≤ 0) | **12.5%** | 大部分有区分度 |

**SJ 的优势在于 spread 而非 signal quality**：SJ median range = 0.57，远大于 logprob 的 0.041。SJ 很少 tied (12.5%)，因此能在更多 instance 上做有效 selection。

### 两者一致性

Logprob-best 和 SJ-best 选中同一个 sample 的比例仅 **14.3%** — 两种信号捕获不同维度的质量。

## 7. Length Bias

| Correlation | Spearman ρ | p |
|------------|-----------|---|
| mean_logprob ↔ n_tokens | +0.339 | 1.3e-118 |
| mean_logprob ↔ NER F1 | +0.305 | 1.6e-95 |
| n_tokens ↔ NER F1 | +0.112 | 7.1e-14 |

- Mean logprob selection F1: 0.6495 (length-normalized)
- Cumulative logprob selection F1: 0.6002 (无 normalization)

Length normalization 至关重要 — cumulative logprob 甚至不如 greedy。但 logprob-best 并不系统性偏好最长样本 (length rank = 0.43, 略偏短)。

## 8. 综合结论

### Ties 是 logprob selection 表现差的主要原因

1. **60% instance logprob 几乎 tied** (range < 0.05)，selection 退化为近随机
2. **在 non-tied 子集上 logprob 有效**：range ≥ 0.05 时显著优于 greedy (p=0.01, +0.027 F1)，甚至优于 SJ
3. **信号强度随 spread 单调递增**：ρ 从 0.08 (tight) 增长到 0.39 (spread)

### 为什么 SJ 整体表现更好

不是因为 SJ 是更好的 quality signal，而是因为 **SJ 几乎不 tied** (仅 12.5%)。SJ 的区分度来自离散的集合比较 (Jaccard)，天然有更大 spread；而 logprob 是连续概率的平均值，在 LLM 对 IE 任务高度自信时被压缩到极窄区间。

### Implication

- Logprob 包含有效的质量信号（在有 spread 时 ρ≈0.39），但被数值压缩问题严重限制
- 两种信号仅 14.3% 一致 → **组合潜力大**
- 未来方向：(a) 放大 logprob spread (temperature scaling, calibration)；(b) logprob + SJ 联合 scoring

# RE Non-zero F1 Conditional Selection (n=397 RE Basis)

## Data
- Source: `exp_012_rerun_1024/samples.jsonl` (Qwen SciERC joint N=8 seed=42 max_tokens=1024)
- Total instances: 551
- **RE basis (gold relations > 0): 397** ✓

## Subset Breakdown (within n=397)

| Subset | n | % |
|--------|---|---|
| Non-zero greedy RE F1 | 238 | 59.9% |
| Zero greedy RE F1 | 159 | 40.1% |
| Zero subset with oracle > 0 | 76/159 | 47.8% |

## Non-zero Greedy RE F1 Subset (n=238)

Greedy RE F1: **0.6743** | Oracle RE F1: **0.7574**

| Signal | Selected F1 | Gain vs Greedy | p-value |
|--------|------------|----------------|---------|
| LP | 0.5995 | -0.0748 | 1.000 |
| FK | 0.6063 | -0.0680 | 1.000 |
| SJ | 0.6035 | -0.0708 | 1.000 |
| VC | 0.5737 | -0.1005 | 1.000 |
| EM | 0.5828 | -0.0914 | 1.000 |

**All 5 signals perform worse than greedy** on the non-zero subset. No signal achieves positive selection gain (p=1.0 for all).

## Full RE Basis (n=397)

Greedy RE F1: **0.4042** | Oracle RE F1: **0.5850**

| Signal | Selected F1 | Gain vs Greedy | p-value |
|--------|------------|----------------|---------|
| LP | 0.3948 | -0.0094 | 1.000 |
| FK | 0.3872 | -0.0171 | 1.000 |
| SJ | 0.3855 | -0.0188 | 1.000 |
| VC | 0.3592 | -0.0451 | 1.000 |
| EM | 0.3718 | -0.0324 | 1.000 |

**All 5 signals also negative on full n=397.** Gains are smaller in magnitude than the non-zero subset because the zero-greedy instances (where signals can only improve) dilute the negative signal.

## Zero Greedy RE F1 Subset (n=159)

Greedy RE F1: **0.0000** | Oracle RE F1: **0.3270**

| Signal | Selected F1 | Gain vs Greedy | p-value |
|--------|------------|----------------|---------|
| LP | 0.0884 | +0.0884 | 0.000* |
| FK | 0.0591 | +0.0591 | 0.000* |
| SJ | 0.0591 | +0.0591 | 0.000* |
| VC | 0.0380 | +0.0380 | 0.008* |
| EM | 0.0560 | +0.0560 | 0.001* |

All signals significant (trivially, since greedy=0 and any non-zero selection is positive).

## Key Takeaways

1. **On instances where greedy already extracts some correct relations (n=238), no consistency signal can beat greedy for RE.** All signals select worse samples, with losses of 7-10 F1 points.
2. **On full n=397**, the net effect is still negative for all signals. The gains from the zero subset are overwhelmed by losses on the non-zero subset.
3. **Oracle gap is large** (greedy 0.4042 → oracle 0.5850 on n=397), confirming that better samples exist in the N=8 pool — the signals just can't find them for RE.
4. **LP is the least harmful** signal on both subsets (smallest negative gain), consistent with it being the best single signal for RE overall.

## Artifacts
- Script: `output/review_round4/analyze_re_nonzero_selection.py`
- JSON results: `output/review_round4/re_nonzero_results_n397.json`

# Logprob Tie Analysis — NER Basis n=529

**Data**: `exp_012_rerun_1024/samples.jsonl` (Qwen SciERC joint, N=8, seed=42, max_tokens=1024)
**Filtering**: 551 total → 22 empty gold NER → **n=529**

---

## 1. Instance-Level Logprob Range

Range = max(mean_logprob) − min(mean_logprob) across 8 samples per instance.

| Stat   | Value    |
|--------|----------|
| Mean   | 0.0622   |
| Median | 0.0401   |
| P25    | 0.0265   |
| P75    | 0.0685   |
| P90    | 0.1221   |
| P95    | 0.1711   |
| Min    | 0.0001   |
| Max    | 0.6083   |

**Instance-level "tied" (range < ε):**

| ε     | Tied instances | % of 529 |
|-------|---------------|----------|
| 0.01  | 6             | 1.1%     |
| 0.05  | 319           | 60.3%    |
| 0.10  | 444           | 83.9%    |
| 0.50  | 526           | 99.4%    |

**Interpretation**: At ε=0.05, 60% of instances have all 8 samples within 0.05 mean_logprob of each other — logprob cannot meaningfully rank them.

---

## 2. Non-Tied Subset Selection Performance

### Full set (n=529)

| Method       | NER F1  |
|-------------|---------|
| Greedy       | 0.6439  |
| LP-best      | 0.6501  |
| SJ-best (MV-Jaccard) | 0.6492  |
| Oracle       | 0.7758  |

### Non-tied subset: range ≥ 0.05 (n=210, 39.7% of instances)

| Method       | NER F1  | vs Greedy   | p-value |
|-------------|---------|-------------|---------|
| Greedy       | 0.5960  | —           | —       |
| LP-best      | 0.6246  | **+0.0286** | **0.010** |
| SJ-best      | 0.6127  | +0.0167     | 0.176   |
| Oracle       | 0.7421  | —           | —       |

- LP-best vs greedy: **+2.9 points, p=0.01** (significant)
- SJ-best vs LP-best: −1.2 points, p=0.37 (not significant)
- LP-best outperforms SJ on the non-tied subset

### Non-tied subset: range ≥ 0.1 (n=85)

| Method       | NER F1  | vs Greedy   | p-value |
|-------------|---------|-------------|---------|
| Greedy       | 0.5779  | —           | —       |
| LP-best      | 0.6148  | +0.0369     | 0.079   |
| SJ-best      | 0.5757  | −0.0022     | 0.923   |
| Oracle       | 0.7316  | —           | —       |

---

## 3. Pairwise Comparison Tie Rate

C(8,2)=28 pairs per instance × 529 instances = **14,812 total pairs**.

Pairwise |diff| stats: mean=0.0228, median=0.0117, P75=0.0260.

| ε      | Tied pairs | % of 14,812 |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| 0.001  | 1,222     | 8.3%        |
| 0.005  | 3,979     | 26.9%       |
| 0.010  | 6,699     | 45.2%       |
| 0.020  | 9,969     | 67.3%       |
| **0.026** | **~11,109** | **~75.0%** |
| 0.050  | 13,259    | 89.5%       |
| 0.100  | 14,312    | 96.6%       |

**论文声明验证**："75% of comparisons are ties" 对应 ε ≈ 0.026（P75 of pairwise diffs = 0.02595）。

这意味着论文所说的"75% tie"不需要特别大的容忍度——mean_logprob 差异的第 75 百分位仅为 0.026，在 per-token logprob 尺度上确实很小。

---

## 4. n=529 vs n=551 对比

| 指标                    | n=551  | n=529  | Δ       |
|------------------------|--------|--------|---------|
| Range mean             | 0.0623 | 0.0622 | −0.0001 |
| Range median           | 0.0413 | 0.0401 | −0.0012 |
| Tied (range<0.05)      | 59.7%  | 60.3%  | +0.6pp  |
| Greedy F1              | 0.6436 | 0.6439 | +0.0003 |
| LP-best F1             | 0.6495 | 0.6501 | +0.0005 |
| SJ-best F1             | 0.6505 | 0.6492 | −0.0013 |
| Pairwise tied (ε=0.05) | 89.2%  | 89.5%  | +0.3pp  |
| P75 pairwise diff      | 0.0263 | 0.0260 | −0.0003 |

**结论**: 基数从 551→529 对所有核心指标影响极小（delta < 0.002）。22 个 empty gold instance 的 logprob 分布与整体一致，不构成偏差来源。

---

## 关键发现

1. **Logprob 信号确实 weak**: 60% 的 instance 在 ε=0.05 下"tied"（8 个样本的 mean_logprob range < 0.05）
2. **但在 non-tied 子集上 logprob 有效**: range ≥ 0.05 的 210 个 instance 上，LP-best 显著优于 greedy（+2.9 F1, p=0.01）
3. **论文 "75% ties" 验证**: 对应 ε ≈ 0.026，在 per-token mean_logprob 尺度上合理
4. **SJ 在 non-tied 子集上不如 LP**: 当 logprob 能区分时，LP 选择优于 SJ（差异不显著但方向一致）
5. **n=529 vs n=551 无实质差异**

---

- 脚本: `output/review_round4/analyze_logprob_ties.py`
- JSON: `output/review_round4/logprob_tie_results_n529.json`

# Logprob Tie Analysis — SciERC NER (exp_012_rerun_1024)

**Data**: Qwen SciERC joint (NER+RE), N=8, seed=42, max_tokens=1024, 551 instances

---

## 1. Logprob Range Distribution

Mean logprob range (max−min across 8 samples per instance):

| Statistic | Value |

**Logprob 值极度集中**：median range 仅 0.041，意味着一半 instance 的 8 个样本 mean_logprob 差异不到 0.04。

## 2. Tie 比例 vs ε 阈值

| ε (range < ε = "tied") | Tied instances | 比例 |
|------------------------|----------------|------|
| 0.001 | 6/551 | 1.1% |
| 0.005 | 8/551 | 1.5% |

| 0.20 | 532/551 | 96.6% |
| 0.50 | 548/551 | 99.5% |

**关键发现**：以 ε=0.05 为标准，**60% 的 instance logprob 值几乎无差异**，选择退化为近似随机。

## 3. 整体 Selection Performance

| Strategy | NER F1 | RE F1 |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Greedy | 0.6436 | 0.4909 |
| Random sample (mean) | 0.6059 | — |
| **Logprob-best** | **0.6495** | 0.4442 |

| Oracle | 0.7775 | — |

Logprob-best 在 NER 上仅比 greedy 高 +0.006，Oracle gap 高达 +0.13，说明 selection 远未饱和。

## 4. Non-Tied 子集上的 Selection Performance

| 阈值 (range ≥) | N (占比) | Greedy F1 | LP-best F1 | Diff | p-value | Win/Lose/Tie |
|---------------|----------|-----------|------------|------|---------|-------------|
| 0.01 | 540 (98%) | 0.6407 | 0.6463 | +0.006 | 0.422 | 60/70/410 |
| 0.02 | 473 (86%) | 0.6276 | 0.6356 | +0.008 | 0.289 | 56/61/356 |
| **0.05** | **222 (40%)** | **0.5863** | **0.6133** | **+0.027** | **0.010** | 29/20/173 |
| 0.10 | 90 (16%) | 0.5680 | 0.6029 | +0.035 | 0.079 | 13/8/69 |
| 0.20 | 19 (3%) | 0.6649 | 0.7108 | +0.046 | 0.295 | 4/1/14 |

**核心结论**：在 logprob 有足够区分度的子集 (range ≥ 0.05, 40% data) 上，logprob selection **显著优于** greedy (p=0.01)。随着区分度增大，logprob 优势单调递增 (+0.027 → +0.035 → +0.046)。

## 5. Within-Instance Logprob-F1 Correlation

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Mean Spearman ρ (mean_logprob ↔ NER F1) | 0.1823 |
| Median ρ | 0.2852 |
| % positive ρ | 64.3% |

Stratified by logprob range:

| Range bin | N instances | Mean ρ | N with variance |
|-----------|------------|--------|----------------|
| < 0.01 | 11 | +0.319 | 4 |
| 0.01–0.05 | 318 | +0.084 | 255 |
| 0.05–0.1 | 132 | +0.252 | 110 |
| **0.1–0.5** | **87** | **+0.390** | 76 |
| ≥ 0.5 | 3 | +0.506 | 3 |

**Logprob 信号随区分度增大而显著增强**：range 在 0.1-0.5 时 ρ=0.39，说明 logprob 本身包含质量信号，但被极窄的数值范围压缩了。

## 6. Structural Consistency (SJ) vs Logprob 对比

### 整体

| Strategy | NER F1 |
|----------|--------|
| Greedy | 0.6436 |
| Logprob-best | 0.6495 |
| SJ-best | 0.6505 |
| Oracle | 0.7775 |

### Non-tied 子集

| Subset | Greedy | LP-best | SJ-best | SJ vs LP (p) |
|--------|--------|---------|---------|--------------|
| range ≥ 0.05 (N=222) | 0.5863 | **0.6133** | 0.6066 | -0.007, p=0.62 |
| range ≥ 0.1 (N=90) | 0.5680 | **0.6029** | 0.5659 | -0.037, p=0.12 |

**意外发现**：在 logprob non-tied 子集上，logprob selection 实际 **优于** SJ。说明 logprob 在有足够 spread 时是有效的 quality signal。

### Tie 对比

| Signal | Tied 比例 | 定义 |
|--------|----------|------|
| Logprob (range < 0.05) | **59.7%** | 数值压缩严重 |
| SJ (range ≤ 0) | **12.5%** | 大部分有区分度 |

**SJ 的优势在于 spread 而非 signal quality**：SJ median range = 0.57，远大于 logprob 的 0.041。SJ 很少 tied (12.5%)，因此能在更多 instance 上做有效 selection。

### 两者一致性

Logprob-best 和 SJ-best 选中同一个 sample 的比例仅 **14.3%** — 两种信号捕获不同维度的质量。

## 7. Length Bias

| Correlation | Spearman ρ | p |
|------------|-----------|---|
| mean_logprob ↔ n_tokens | +0.339 | 1.3e-118 |
| mean_logprob ↔ NER F1 | +0.305 | 1.6e-95 |
| n_tokens ↔ NER F1 | +0.112 | 7.1e-14 |

- Mean logprob selection F1: 0.6495 (length-normalized)
- Cumulative logprob selection F1: 0.6002 (无 normalization)

Length normalization 至关重要 — cumulative logprob 甚至不如 greedy。但 logprob-best 并不系统性偏好最长样本 (length rank = 0.43, 略偏短)。

## 8. 综合结论

### Ties 是 logprob selection 表现差的主要原因

1. **60% instance logprob 几乎 tied** (range < 0.05)，selection 退化为近随机
2. **在 non-tied 子集上 logprob 有效**：range ≥ 0.05 时显著优于 greedy (p=0.01, +0.027 F1)，甚至优于 SJ
3. **信号强度随 spread 单调递增**：ρ 从 0.08 (tight) 增长到 0.39 (spread)

### 为什么 SJ 整体表现更好

不是因为 SJ 是更好的 quality signal，而是因为 **SJ 几乎不 tied** (仅 12.5%)。SJ 的区分度来自离散的集合比较 (Jaccard)，天然有更大 spread；而 logprob 是连续概率的平均值，在 LLM 对 IE 任务高度自信时被压缩到极窄区间。

### Implication

- Logprob 包含有效的质量信号（在有 spread 时 ρ≈0.39），但被数值压缩问题严重限制
- 两种信号仅 14.3% 一致 → **组合潜力大**
- 未来方向：(a) 放大 logprob spread (temperature scaling, calibration)；(b) logprob + SJ 联合 scoring

3	\paragraph{Practical recommendations.}
4	For per-instance quality ranking, entity voting provides the strongest rank correlation ($\rho{=}0.38$), though exact match leads binary discrimination (AUROC${=}0.749$); under conditional filtering, EM leads on both NER and RE ($\rho{=}0.360$, $0.417$).

6	When model capability is insufficient (WNUT-17), all signals converge toward non-significant conditional correlations (Table~\ref{tab:wnut}).
7	
8	\paragraph{Why the gap exists: two layers.}
9	\textit{Layer 1 (structural):} Four of five signals are instance-level aggregates that assign a single score per input; they cannot rank candidates by construction.
10	Consensus-proximity selection (\S\ref{sec:evaluation}) does not recover per-sample discrimination (Table~\ref{tab:selection}).
11	\textit{Layer 2 (empirical):} Log-probability, the only per-sample signal, also fails to exploit the 13--18~pp oracle headroom.
12	Under constrained decoding, logprob scores are severely compressed: 60\% of instances have a within-sample range below 0.05, and 75\% of pairwise comparisons are effective ties ($|\Delta|{<}0.026$; Appendix~\ref{app:logprob_ties}).
13	In the non-tied 40\%, logprob selection significantly outperforms greedy ($+2.9$~pp, $p{=}0.01$), confirming the signal carries useful information but is resolution-limited.
14	The common root is that quality estimation ranks \textit{instances}, while sample selection requires ranking \textit{candidates within a single instance}---a finer granularity that neither instance-level aggregation nor token-level confidence provides.
15	Diversity-stratified analysis confirms the gap persists even among high-diversity instances (Appendix~\ref{app:diversity}); RE miscalibration (ECE 0.109--0.339; Appendix~\ref{app:calibration}) may compound this failure.
16	
17	\paragraph{Connection to MBR decoding.}
18	Our selection strategies instantiate minimum Bayes risk (MBR) decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, muller2021understanding}: each selects $\hat{y} = \arg\max_{y_i} \sum_{j \neq i} U(y_i, y_j)$ with utility $U$ defined by SJ, EM, or entity overlap.
19	Despite MBR's success in machine translation \cite{freitag2022high}, all variants fail here because the utility functions correlate with F1 at the instance level but not within a single instance---the mathematical essence of the correlation-selection gap.
20	
21	\paragraph{Methodological implications.}
22	The decoupling of quality estimation ($\rho$), binary discrimination (AUROC), and sample selection (best-of-$N$ F1) means evaluating on a single metric risks selecting the wrong signal for the intended use case.
23	Effective selection likely requires per-sample signals such as trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers}; $N$-scaling analysis (Appendix~\ref{app:additional}) shows $N{=}8$ captures most quality estimation benefit.

\textit{Layer 2 (empirical):} Log-probability, the only per-sample signal, also fails to exploit the 13--18~pp oracle headroom.
Under constrained decoding, logprob scores are severely compressed: 60\% of instances have a within-sample range below 0.05, and 75\% of pairwise comparisons are effective ties ($|\Delta|{<}0.026$; Appendix~\ref{app:logprob_ties}).
In the non-tied 40\%, logprob selection significantly outperforms greedy ($+2.9$~pp, $p{=}0.01$), confirming the signal carries useful information but is resolution-limited.
The common root is that quality estimation ranks \textit{instances}, while sample selection requires ranking \textit{candidates within a single instance}---a finer granularity that neither instance-level aggregation nor token-level confidence provides.
Diversity-stratified analysis confirms the gap persists even among high-diversity instances (Appendix~\ref{app:diversity}); RE miscalibration (ECE 0.109--0.339; Appendix~\ref{app:calibration}) may compound this failure.

\paragraph{Connection to MBR decoding.}
Our selection strategies instantiate minimum Bayes risk (MBR) decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, muller2021understanding}: each selects $\hat{y} = \arg\max_{y_i} \sum_{j \neq i} U(y_i, y_j)$ with utility $U$ defined by SJ, EM, or entity overlap.
Despite MBR's success in machine translation \cite{freitag2022high}, all variants fail here because the utility functions correlate with F1 at the instance level but not within a single instance---the mathematical essence of the correlation-selection gap.

\paragraph{Methodological implications.}
The decoupling of quality estimation ($\rho$), binary discrimination (AUROC), and sample selection (best-of-$N$ F1) means evaluating on a single metric risks selecting the wrong signal for the intended use case.
Effective selection likely requires per-sample signals such as trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers}; $N$-scaling analysis (Appendix~\ref{app:additional}) shows $N{=}8$ captures most quality estimation benefit.

\paragraph{Temperature sensitivity.}
SJ NER $\rho$ shifts from 0.388 ($T{=}0.7$) to 0.360 ($T{=}1.0$), a difference of 0.028 whose bootstrap confidence interval includes zero.
FK shows mixed behavior: NER $\rho$ drops by 0.054, while RE $\rho$ increases by 0.091, likely reflecting reduced diversity at lower temperature interacting differently across tasks.
Across all comparisons, the SJ--FK relative ordering is preserved at both temperatures on NER (0.388 vs.\ 0.321 at $T{=}0.7$; 0.360 vs.\ 0.267 at $T{=}1.0$), indicating a stable signal hierarchy despite numerically small temperature effects.

\paragraph{Sample size scaling.}
Increasing from $N{=}8$ to $N{=}16$ improves SJ on Qwen SciERC NER: $\rho$ rises from 0.360 to $0.412{\pm}0.025$ (three seeds: 0.428, 0.424, 0.384), a gain of $+0.052$.
The magnitude of $N$-scaling gains is setting-dependent---LLaMA SciERC NER yields $+0.016$ and Qwen CoNLL NER $+0.014$---though the direction is consistently positive.
LLaMA CoNLL exhibits the most uniform scaling: all four consistency signals gain $\Delta\rho{\approx}{+}0.030$ (range: $+0.027$ to $+0.032$) while logprob gains only $+0.003$ (Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}).
FK $N$-scaling is inconsistent: degradation on SciERC ($-0.007$ to $-0.019$) but improvement on CoNLL with LLaMA ($+0.027$), suggesting sensitivity to both model and task characteristics.
Voting confidence $N$-scaling is consistently positive ($+0.005$ on Qwen CoNLL, $+0.018$ on LLaMA SciERC, $+0.062$ on Qwen SciERC), while logprob is approximately $N$-invariant ($\Delta{\leq}0.021$).
SJ, EM, and voting confidence scale consistently across all tested settings; only FK shows setting-dependent variation, suggesting that structural and binary-agreement signals are the most robust to $N$.

\paragraph{Cross-architecture transfer.}
LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct replicates the structural-over-surface ordering on SciERC NER (SJ $\rho{=}0.363$, FK $\rho{=}0.327$).

\section{Additional Analyses}\label{app:additional}

\paragraph{Per-relation diagnostic.}
RE signal degradation is relation-specific.
\textsc{Feature-Of} has near-zero correlation ($\rho{=}0.004$), while \textsc{Hyponym-Of} achieves $\rho{=}0.646$.
The primary bottleneck is entity span errors, which account for 55.5\% of RE false negatives---a prerequisite failure that consistency signals cannot detect, as they measure agreement among equally incorrect extractions.
We note that RE analysis relies on a single dataset (SciERC); generalization to other RE benchmarks remains to be validated.

\paragraph{Capability stratification.}
For NER, SJ effectiveness scales with structural complexity: on SciERC instances with 6+ entities, $\rho{=}0.547$, compared to $\rho{=}0.415$ for 1--2 entities.
The SJ advantage over logprob remains stable across sentence-length quartiles ($\Delta\rho{\approx}0.08$--$0.20$).
For RE, SJ $\rho$ increases monotonically with sentence length (Q1: 0.110 $\to$ Q4: 0.473; Fisher $z$-test $p{=}0.004$), indicating that longer, more relation-dense sentences provide richer structure for consistency-based estimation.
Both proxies are weakly correlated with F1 ($|r|{<}0.15$), confirming they capture input complexity rather than directly predicting output quality; however, entity count and sentence length are themselves moderately correlated ($\rho{=}0.650$), so they reflect overlapping rather than independent complexity dimensions.
For RE, entity count and relation count are strongly correlated ($\rho{=}0.769$) and thus reflect a single structural complexity dimension rather than independent axes.
On the high-complexity RE subset ($n{=}81$, high relation count), signals improve substantially: Voting reaches $\rho{=}0.630$, logprob $\rho{=}0.554$, and SJ $\rho{=}0.502$---all far above the full-set levels.
Richer relational structure provides more signal for consistency-based estimation, complementing the task-level boundary established by WNUT-17: structural signals are most effective within a ``sweet spot'' of sufficient model capability and sufficient output complexity.

\paragraph{Length vs.\ log-probability.}
Figure~\ref{fig:length_logprob_scatter} shows that mean log-probability is weakly positively correlated with output length (NER: $\rho{=}0.386$, $n{=}4{,}232$; RE: $\rho{=}0.326$, $n{=}3{,}176$), ruling out length-penalty confounding as an explanation for logprob's selection failure: longer outputs receive \textit{higher}, not lower, token-averaged log-probability under constrained decoding.

\label{fig:length_logprob_scatter}
\end{figure}

\paragraph{Evaluation circularity.}
Leave-one-out SJ (LOO-SJ), which excludes the target sample when computing confidence, yields $\Delta\rho{=}{-}0.014$ relative to standard SJ (a correlation-level difference), with a maximum per-instance score difference of $3.1{\times}10^{-4}$ (negligible at the individual prediction level).
Evaluation circularity is negligible.

\paragraph{Conditional filtering details.}
On LLaMA conditional RE (non-zero F1 instances), SJ recovers to $\rho{=}0.405$ while FK drops to $\rho{=}0.259$, confirming that structural advantage is robust across both models and evaluation conditions.
At $N{=}16$, the divergence persists: SJ maintains $\rho{=}0.308$ on conditional RE while logprob drops to $\rho{=}{-}0.026$.
EM ranks first across all four tested conditional configurations---SciERC NER ($\rho{=}0.360$), CoNLL Qwen $N{=}16$ ($\rho{=}0.466$), CoNLL LLaMA 3-seed ($\rho{=}0.462$), and SciERC RE ($\rho{=}0.417$)---despite full-set rankings ranging from \#1 (CoNLL Qwen) to \#5 (SciERC RE).
On the full set, EM is diluted by trivial agreement: instances where all $N$ samples produce identical (possibly incorrect) outputs receive EM${=}1$ regardless of quality, compressing the signal's dynamic range.
On the conditional set---where the model demonstrably produces varied outputs---exact agreement becomes the strongest quality signal.
The margin over SJ is largest on RE ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.171$), where compound extraction decisions amplify output variability, and smallest on CoNLL LLaMA ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.002$), where all signals converge near $\rho{\approx}0.46$.

Voting achieves $\rho{=}0.724$ (AUROC${=}0.913$) on the full set, but conditional analysis (non-zero F1 instances) reveals this is entirely driven by the zero/non-zero boundary: conditional $\rho{=}0.038$ ($p{=}0.49$).
Logprob shows the reverse pattern: full-set $\rho{=}{-}0.410$ but conditional $\rho{=}0.350$, the highest among all signals on the conditional set.

\paragraph{Diminishing returns of $N$-scaling.}
Our $N{=}8$ and $N{=}16$ comparisons (Table~\ref{tab:robustness}) characterize the marginal value of additional samples for test-time scaling \cite{brown2024monkeys, snell2024scaling}.
For quality estimation, structural signals benefit consistently but sublinearly: SJ $\rho$ improves by $+0.052$ (Qwen SciERC, 3-seed mean) and $+0.032$ (LLaMA CoNLL, 3-seed mean) when doubling from $N{=}8$ to $N{=}16$, while log-probability is approximately $N$-invariant ($\Delta\rho{\leq}0.021$).
Structural signals leverage $\binom{N}{2}$ pairwise comparisons (28 pairs at $N{=}8$, 120 at $N{=}16$), but the $\rho$ improvement is far less than proportional, indicating diminishing information per additional comparison.
This asymmetry gives structural signals a relative advantage in the compute-constrained regime: at $N{=}8$, SJ already achieves $\rho{=}0.431$ on LLaMA CoNLL (vs.\ logprob $\rho{=}0.307$, $\Delta{=}{+}0.124$), and the gap \textit{widens} at $N{=}16$ ($\Delta{=}{+}0.153$) because structural signals continue to benefit from additional pairwise evidence while logprob does not.
For sample selection, additional samples increase the oracle upper bound---more draws raise the probability of a high-quality candidate---but signal-based selection remains flat because the selector's inability to identify the best candidate is a granularity limitation, not a sample size limitation.
The practical implication is that $N{=}8$ captures most of the achievable quality estimation benefit; further scaling widens rather than closes the correlation-selection gap absent stronger per-sample selectors.

On the 44\% of Qwen SciERC instances with high diversity (${\geq}4$ unique outputs among 8 samples, $n{=}232$), oracle headroom reaches $+$16.3~pp, yet all consistency-based signals (SJ, FK, EM, Voting) select at or below greedy, and logprob---the only per-sample signal---achieves merely $+$0.8~pp.

83	EM emerges as the strongest conditional signal on both NER ($\rho{=}0.360$) and RE ($\rho{=}0.417$), while Voting and FK drop substantially (Voting NER: $0.379{\to}0.300$; FK NER: $0.267{\to}0.176$).
84	Logprob RE collapses to $\rho{=}0.011$, confirming its full-set correlation was driven by zero/non-zero separation.
85	This creates a natural complementarity: Voting and SJ are preferred on the full set, while EM provides the most precise ranking within the non-trivial subset (see Appendix~\ref{app:additional} for details).

120	Despite strong quality estimation, confidence signals yield limited gains when used for best-of-$N$ selection (Table~\ref{tab:selection}, Figure~\ref{fig:selection_gap}).
121	Four of five signals are instance-level aggregates that assign a single score per input regardless of which sample is evaluated; they cannot rank candidates by construction.
122	The non-trivial question is whether log-probability---the only per-sample signal---can exploit the oracle headroom.
123	We anchor this analysis on SciERC, where output diversity is substantial: only 11--18\% of instances produce identical outputs across all $N{=}8$ samples, with 39--43\% unique outputs per instance (mean 3.5 distinct outputs), per-sample F1 standard deviation of 0.11--0.14, and mean pairwise SJ of 0.703.
124	
125	\paragraph{No significant improvement over greedy.}
126	We exclude 22 instances with empty gold annotations, yielding $n{=}529$ for statistical analysis.
127	We evaluate statistical significance using instance-level paired bootstrap resampling ($B{=}10{,}000$, with replacement) over these instances, reporting 95\% percentile CIs.
128	The three random seeds (42, 123, 456) refer to independent inference runs; we average $\rho$ across seeds and report the bootstrap $p$-value of the paired difference (best signal vs.\ greedy).
129	On NER, the oracle (0.776) reveals 13.2~pp of headroom above greedy (0.644).
130	Logprob achieves the highest selection F1 (0.650, +0.6~pp), but this is not statistically significant ($p{=}0.39$; 95\% CI: [$-$3.0, +4.2]~pp; Cohen's $d{=}0.038$; sign test: 61W/70L, win\%${=}$46.6\%).
131	On RE, the gap is complete: the best signal (logprob, 0.395) falls below greedy (0.404, $-0.9$\,pp, $p{=}0.80$), while 18.1~pp of oracle headroom remains.
132	TOST equivalence testing confirms that most signals are statistically indistinguishable from greedy: on NER, SJ and logprob are equivalent within ${\pm}2$~pp; on RE, EM and Voting fail equivalence even at ${\pm}5$~pp due to systematic underperformance (Table~\ref{tab:tost}, Appendix~\ref{app:diversity}).
133	Voting ($\rho{=}0.379$, the best quality estimator) selects to only 0.634 on NER---\textit{below} greedy.
134	The gap extends to CoNLL and WNUT-17 (Table~\ref{tab:cross_selection}), though these cases are less informative for selection analysis: CoNLL exhibits a ceiling effect where 57--88\% of instances produce identical outputs across all $N$ samples (greedy F1 already ${\approx}$0.91--0.92), and WNUT-17 is dominated by the capability boundary (52\% zero F1; \S\ref{sec:qe_results}).
135	The SciERC results, where meaningful per-sample variance exists, provide the strongest evidence that instance-level signals cannot discriminate among diverse candidates.
136	
137	\paragraph{Quality estimation $\neq$ output selection.}
138	Instance-level confidence signals predict \textit{which inputs} the model handles reliably, not \textit{which output} among $N$ candidates is best.
139	When per-sample variance is low relative to instance-level difficulty, even perfect quality estimation cannot discriminate among near-identical candidates.
140	This gap has direct consequences for test-time scaling in IE \cite{brown2024monkeys, snell2024scaling}: closing it likely requires per-sample signals such as trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers}.

144	\label{sec:robustness_main}

146	Consistency-based signals show robust performance across $T{\in}\{0.7, 1.0\}$ (SJ NER $\Delta\rho{=}0.028$, bootstrap CI includes zero) and sublinear gains from $N{=}8$ to $N{=}16$, with structural signals maintaining their advantage over logprob across all settings ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.135$ to ${+}0.175$; Table~\ref{tab:robustness}, Appendix~\ref{app:robustness}).
